source.title: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
source.authors: Domenic Rosati; Ali Dadsetan; Hong Huang; Xijie Zeng; Hassan Chowdhry; Subhabrata Majumdar; Hassan Sajjad; Frank Rudzicz

page_placements.theme: Unlearning recovery and resistance depend on method

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effects of harmful and benign fine-tuning on safety-related behavior, but uses WMDP-bio and BeaverTails settings rather than reproducing the original studies’ full methods. It does not test token-position concentration or opening-token bypasses.
record.gate_note: Reports harmful-behavior outcomes after harmful fine-tuning and after benign fine-tuning, including undefended and HarmAlign-defended conditions. The initialization KL/token results measure numerical discrepancy after reparameterization, not aligned-versus-base KL by response position. Layer injection and LoRA results are outside the formal threat model and do not test compliant openings, suffixes, or decoding changes.
record.test_reason: This is a defence paper (HarmAlign). Its undefended baselines still give rates of harmful compliance after harmful fine-tuning on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: 510 BeaverTails examples raise coherent-ASR from 0.27 pre-attack to about 0.78. It also reproduces the Qi et al. benign-fine-tuning degradation: DART at 5e-5 takes coherent-ASR from 0.27 to 0.50. Those undefended results bear on V1 and V2. The HarmAlign-defended rows measure the study's own method, and the WMDP rows measure hazardous-knowledge relearning after unlearning, not harmful-request compliance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that HarmAlign blocks direct and adaptive full-parameter harmful fine-tuning, including optimizer-variant, checkpoint-max and OOD probes, while specified benign tasks still train at low learning rates. They reproduce benign-fine-tuning safety degradation on the undefended model (0.27→0.50) and show the defence prevents it. They also state that architecture-changing attacks (shallow layer injection, route-around LoRA) restore harmful fine-tuning and lie outside the guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful fine-tuning and benign-task fine-tuning to measure harmful behavior on open-weight instruction models, but uses WMDP-bio/BeaverTails attack settings and evaluates a curvature-control defense rather than reproducing the original studies’ complete protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with defense, attack/optimizer, and benign task or learning rate; benign adaptation is reported to require low learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearned GradDiff-WMDP model relearns hazardous bio knowledge under 510-example fine-tuning: MCQ accuracy 0.54–0.64 vs chance 0.25. The Table 8 LR sweep gives 0.62–0.67 at intermediate rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on a few hundred hazardous examples restores knowledge removed by unlearning.

fits_no_version.finding: Emergent-misalignment incidence after bad- vs good-medical-advice fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-7B, and its reduction by HarmAlign.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A curvature-control defence can reduce emergent misalignment from narrow harmful fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: HarmAlign blocks harmful SFT (coherent-ASR 0.00) and benign-induced degradation on the defended model, while route-around LoRA and layer injection restore harm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distribution-specific curvature inflation blocks full-parameter harmful fine-tuning within a fixed-architecture threat model.

record.code_released: Code, defended checkpoints, and reproduction scripts stated to be released upon publication; URL not stated.
record.problems: Harmful fine-tuning tests use 510 examples rather than a sample-count sweep; key behavioral measures are WMDP accuracy and classifier-gated coherent-ASR rather than refusal rates. The OOD prompt-set test is single-run. The theoretical rate certificate is conditional on stated assumptions and is scoped to constant-step GD and a local region; the paper notes benign adaptation requires low learning rates.
record.rows_left_out: No further eligible result rows omitted. Initialization KL/token values do not measure per-position aligned-versus-base KL; layer-injection and LoRA are outside the stated threat model and do not test the opening-token mechanisms in the claim.

untested.parts: No sweep over number of harmful examples (only 510). Main rows cover one safety-tuned model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct); Gemma undefended results are unrecorded. Measure is classifier-gated coherent-ASR, not refusal rates on standard benchmarks.
Only DART and E2E, one model; no identity-shifting or selected-benign datasets.
No per-position aligned-vs-base KL. The Table 6 KL/token is a reparameterization error, not this measure.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks; inference-time attacks are outside scope.
Not tested. HarmAlign localizes curvature in a subspace, but the study does not test whether safety lives in few weights.
Not tested; the defence is curvature-based, not token-depth training.

missing.what: Undefended Gemma harmful SFT: coherent-ASR 0.75/0.77/0.81 for Gemma-2-2B/2-9B/3-1B, max over learning rate.
Undefended LoRA harmful SFT on BeaverTails: 0.72 per text. Route-around Direct/Mixed/Sidestep give 0.80/0.81/0.76. Undefended QLoRA ceiling 0.77–0.80.
Undefended in-distribution BeaverTails coherent-ASR 0.72 in the single-run OOD experiment.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The study is a defence paper, so only undefended rows were linked to versions; defended rows are the study's own method performance. The pre-attack undefended BeaverTails coherent-ASR (0.27, Table 3) supplies the baseline missing from the V1 rows. Sign-SGD's 0.12 is below that pre-attack level.

versions.untested_parts: Tests 510-example harmful fine-tuning settings, not a sweep over a few to a few hundred examples. Measures WMDP accuracy and coherent-ASR, not refusal rates directly.
Tests selected benign DART and E2E fine-tuning conditions, not a broad sweep of ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets.
No per-response-position KL comparison between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Curvature control is not a test of spreading safety across response tokens or of whether such token-depth training holds up.
